title: The lane is driveable and shouts like the game; a run is a fixed population that scores itself against the 60fps line
context: Owner feedback on the lane: the shader wobble looks better, but did it gain fps; the tank was skidding and should run straight and be drivable by the tester; and the ram chain should appear as it does IN GAME, not only as telemetry, because this is a gameplay-feel test as much as a measurement. Then: after a run — all units destroyed or passed out of frame — show a telemetry score with max, average and median percent of a 60 fps frame, visually, recordable, and comparable against the next run.
outcome: FPS answer, measured rather than claimed: no meaningful gain. The three authored creatures cost ZERO before because they had no TICKS entry and never animated in gameplay, so the port bought animation, not frames. The only real saving is the two swimmers leaving the CPU, worth 1.75 us/unit/frame for scoutufo (170 dots) and 3.81 us for shellback (400 dots) — 0.35 ms and 0.76 ms respectively at 200 alive, against a 16.67 ms budget. The tank now holds one heading: a first cut yawed it off a sine, which read as skidding because the hull pointed one way and travelled another. Default drive is manual on WASD/arrows with held-key state rather than key repeat. The shout layer is the game's own: .callout, .co-milestone and the .combobox [data-tier] ladder all come from styles.css and the pack variables from fonts.js applyFontPack, so the lab wears the real phosphors, the real rungs and the tier-5 flicker, and a typeface decision still reaches it without a second edit. A run seats `count` bodies ONCE and ends when the last is rammed, escaped or blocked — free play still recycles, because a number taken off an endless stream describes the sampler rather than the work. The scorecard reports two distributions side by side: wall-clock frame gap (max, p95, median, late-frame count and percent, each also as percent of a 60 fps frame) and the GPU timer, explicitly labelled indicative. Both are shown because they disagree: TIME_ELAPSED_EXT through ANGLE reported a 5.7 ms median and 38 ms p95 for 150 bodies while a gl.finish probe on the same scene read 0.8 ms for 420, so the card carries the one number that cannot be argued with next to the one that can. A per-frame bar chart against the 60 fps line shows the shape of the run, clamped at 4x budget so a single hitch does not flatten every other bar. Runs can be kept (up to four, persisted through src/storage.js) and are rendered as columns beside the current one. Found by measuring: the readout's own cost probe renders the scene six more times and blocks on gl.finish each time, and at 0.4 s intervals was landing a deliberate hitch inside the distribution the run exists to measure — late frames fell from 12% to 8% and the worst gap from 188 ms to 99 ms once it stands down during a scored run.
alternatives: Report only the GPU timer: rejected, it disagreed with a direct probe by roughly 7x and nothing in the card would have shown that.
Report only wall-clock frame gaps: rejected, they cannot separate GPU work from vsync or compositor jank; the pair is what makes either readable.
Keep recycling bodies during a scored run: rejected, an endless stream has no end to measure to.
Sample with gl.finish every frame: rejected, it distorts the frame it measures — which is exactly the bug that was found and fixed.
evidence: Node microbenchmark of swimWave for the scoutufo and shellback point counts, 30,000 iterations after warmup.

scripts/browser-test.mjs swarm-study now asserts the study opens under the tester's hand, the ladder shows and climbs and wears the shout pack, and that a finished run accounts for every body (rammed + escaped + blocked === count), sampled wall-clock frames, and can be kept, compared and cleared.

Headless run, 260 phages: 42.2 s, all 260 rammed, chain of 260, 2725 kg, frame gap median 16.7 ms and p95 23.5 ms with 8% late, GPU timer median 6.32 ms. Headless Chrome has no real vsync, so its late-frame share is environmental; the card exists so that is visible rather than assumed.
npm test, npm run check, npm run build, npm run test:browser and node scripts/browser-test.mjs --dist all pass.
